instructions: Ambiguity hunt. Choose the answer labels, then argue the strongest case for one wrong option in case {label, text}. Set flag to one sentence when that case is defensible or a constraint is missing, else null.

items.stem: A company runs a web application in the us-east-1 Region and keeps a static maintenance page in an Amazon S3 bucket that is configured as a website. The company creates Amazon Route 53 failover records for www.example.com. The primary record is an alias record for an Application Load Balancer. The secondary record points to the S3 website endpoint. The company must ensure that Route 53 sends users to the maintenance page when the application cannot serve requests. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.label: A
options.text: Turn on Evaluate Target Health for the primary record, so that Route 53 uses the health of the resource that the record points to.

options.label: B
options.text: Create a Route 53 health check that sends HTTP requests to the primary endpoint, and associate the health check with the primary record.

options.label: C
options.text: Create a Route 53 health check of the S3 website endpoint, and associate the health check with the secondary record.

options.label: D
options.text: Run a scheduled AWS Lambda function that tests the application every minute and repoints the primary record to the S3 website endpoint on failure.

items.stem: A company has a hybrid network. Its data center connects to a VPC in the eu-west-1 Region through an AWS Direct Connect dedicated connection. The VPC is associated with an Amazon Route 53 private hosted zone named corp.internal. DNS servers in the data center host the zone onprem.corp. Servers in the data center must resolve names in corp.internal. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.label: A
options.text: Create an inbound Resolver endpoint in the VPC, and configure the data center DNS servers to forward corp.internal queries to the endpoint's IP addresses.

options.label: B
options.text: Create an outbound Resolver endpoint and a forwarding rule for onprem.corp that targets the data center DNS servers, and associate the rule with the VPC.

options.label: C
options.text: Configure the data center DNS servers to forward corp.internal queries to the VPC Resolver address at the base of the VPC CIDR range plus two.

options.label: D
options.text: Run DNS forwarder software on EC2 instances in two Availability Zones, and configure both networks to forward queries for the other zone to them.

items.stem: A company hosts the DNS records for its domain, example.com, in an Amazon Route 53 public hosted zone. The company's website runs on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer. The marketing team wants users to open the website by typing example.com in a browser, without the www prefix. The DNS answer for example.com must keep working when the load balancer scales. Which DNS record should a solutions architect create in the hosted zone to meet these requirements?

options.label: A
options.text: An alias record of type A for example.com that points to the Application Load Balancer.

options.label: B
options.text: An A record for example.com whose value is the current IP addresses of the Application Load Balancer.

options.label: C
options.text: A CNAME record for example.com whose value is the DNS name of the Application Load Balancer.

options.label: D
options.text: An NS record for example.com whose value is the DNS name of the Application Load Balancer.

items.stem: A media company serves users around the world from Application Load Balancers in eu-west-1 and us-east-1. Because of distribution rights, the company uses Amazon Route 53 geolocation records: users in Europe go to eu-west-1, and users in North America go to us-east-1. Users in South America, and some users whose location cannot be identified, get no answer from DNS. These users must be served from us-east-1. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.label: A
options.text: Add a geolocation record for each remaining continent and a record with the location Default, all pointing to the us-east-1 load balancer.

options.label: B
options.text: Add a latency record with the same name that points to the us-east-1 load balancer, so that it answers when no geolocation record matches.

options.label: C
options.text: Add a geolocation record with the location Default that points to the us-east-1 load balancer, and keep the existing records.

options.label: D
options.text: Add a geolocation record for each remaining continent, and point each new continent record to the us-east-1 load balancer.

items.stem: A company runs a web application behind an Application Load Balancer in us-east-1 and keeps a warm standby copy behind another Application Load Balancer in us-west-2. Amazon Route 53 hosts the company's public DNS records. The cross-Region recovery plan must move users to us-west-2 when the application in us-east-1 fails, even if the Route 53 control plane is impaired during the event. Which combination of steps will make the plan the MOST resilient? (Select TWO.)

options.label: A
options.text: Create failover alias records in advance, with the us-east-1 load balancer as the primary and the us-west-2 load balancer as the secondary.

options.label: B
options.text: During the event, change the weights of weighted alias records so that the us-west-2 load balancer gets all the traffic.

options.label: C
options.text: Before the event, move the hosted zone from us-east-1 to us-west-2 so that DNS changes can be made in us-west-2.

options.label: D
options.text: Base the health of the primary record on a health check or on Evaluate Target Health, so that Route 53 fails over by itself.

options.label: E
options.text: During the event, create a new record that points the application's domain name to the us-west-2 load balancer.

items.stem: A company runs a web application in the us-east-1 Region and keeps a static maintenance page in an Amazon S3 bucket that is configured as a website. The company creates Amazon Route 53 failover records for www.example.com. The primary record is an A record with the Elastic IP address of one EC2 instance. The secondary record points to the S3 website endpoint. The company must ensure that Route 53 sends users to the maintenance page when the application cannot serve requests. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.label: A
options.text: Run a scheduled AWS Lambda function that tests the application every minute and repoints the primary record to the S3 website endpoint on failure.

options.label: B
options.text: Create a Route 53 health check that sends HTTP requests to the primary endpoint, and associate the health check with the primary record.

options.label: C
options.text: Create a Route 53 health check of the S3 website endpoint, and associate the health check with the secondary record.

options.label: D
options.text: Turn on Evaluate Target Health for the primary record, so that Route 53 uses the health of the resource that the record points to.

items.stem: A company has a hybrid network. Its data center connects to a VPC in the eu-west-1 Region through an AWS Direct Connect dedicated connection. The VPC is associated with an Amazon Route 53 private hosted zone named corp.internal. DNS servers in the data center host the zone onprem.corp. EC2 instances in the VPC must resolve names in onprem.corp. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.label: A
options.text: Run DNS forwarder software on EC2 instances in two Availability Zones, and configure both networks to forward queries for the other zone to them.

options.label: B
options.text: Configure the data center DNS servers to forward corp.internal queries to the VPC Resolver address at the base of the VPC CIDR range plus two.

options.label: C
options.text: Create an inbound Resolver endpoint in the VPC, and configure the data center DNS servers to forward corp.internal queries to the endpoint's IP addresses.

options.label: D
options.text: Create an outbound Resolver endpoint and a forwarding rule for onprem.corp that targets the data center DNS servers, and associate the rule with the VPC.

items.stem: A company serves its website at the edge through an Amazon CloudFront distribution. IPv6 is turned on for the distribution, and example.com is an alternate domain name of the distribution. The company hosts example.com in an Amazon Route 53 public hosted zone. Users on IPv4 networks and users on IPv6 networks must reach the website at example.com. Which combination of actions should the company take in the hosted zone to meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead? (Select TWO.)

options.label: A
options.text: Create a CNAME record for example.com whose value is the domain name of the CloudFront distribution.

options.label: B
options.text: Create a Lambda function that rewrites A and AAAA records for example.com with the distribution's addresses every minute.

options.label: C
options.text: Create an alias record of type AAAA for example.com that points to the domain name of the CloudFront distribution.

options.label: D
options.text: Create an A record for example.com that lists the IP addresses that the distribution's domain name returns today.

options.label: E
options.text: Create an alias record of type A for example.com that points to the domain name of the CloudFront distribution.

items.stem: A company registered the domain example.com with a third-party registrar, which also hosts the DNS records today. The company wants to migrate the DNS service for example.com to Amazon Route 53. Because of a contract, the domain registration must stay with the current registrar. Users on the internet must keep resolving the company's website during the change. What should the company do?

options.label: A
options.text: Create a Route 53 public hosted zone with the records, then change the domain's name servers at the registrar to the hosted zone's name servers.

options.label: B
options.text: Transfer the domain registration to Route 53 first, then create the records in the hosted zone that Route 53 creates for the domain.

options.label: C
options.text: Create a Route 53 private hosted zone with the records, and associate the hosted zone with the VPC that runs the website.

options.label: D
options.text: Create the records in Route 53, and add a CNAME record at the registrar that points example.com to a Route 53 name server.

items.stem: A small team runs version 1 of a web application behind one Application Load Balancer. The team deploys version 2 behind a second Application Load Balancer in the same Region. The team wants about 10 percent of users to reach version 2 first, a larger share during the next week, and a quick way to send every user back to version 1 if errors appear. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.label: A
options.text: Create multivalue answer alias records for the two load balancers, and change how many records each version has to shift users.

options.label: B
options.text: Run a scheduled script that switches a simple alias record between the two load balancers to approximate the share of users.

options.label: C
options.text: Create weighted alias records for the two load balancers with weights of 90 and 10, and change the weights to shift users or roll back.

options.label: D
options.text: Create failover alias records with the version 1 load balancer as the primary and the version 2 load balancer as the secondary.

items.stem: A company runs the same stateless web application in us-east-1 and eu-west-1, behind an Application Load Balancer in each Region. The application has users around the world. The company hosts its DNS records in a Route 53 public hosted zone. Each user must be served from the Region that gives that user the lowest latency. Which routing configuration for www.example.com will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.label: A
options.text: Latency alias records for the two load balancers, one record in each Region, with Evaluate Target Health turned on for both records.

options.label: B
options.text: Geolocation alias records: a Europe record that points to the eu-west-1 load balancer, and a Default record for the us-east-1 load balancer.

options.label: C
options.text: IP-based records with a CIDR collection that the team keeps current with the client IP ranges that each of the two Regions must serve.

options.label: D
options.text: Weighted alias records for the two load balancers with equal weights, so that each Region receives half of the DNS queries for the name.

items.stem: A company will migrate www.example.com from web servers in its data center to an Application Load Balancer next Saturday. In the Route 53 public hosted zone, www.example.com is an A record with a TTL of 86,400 seconds. Users must move to the new site with minimal downtime, and the team must be able to roll back quickly if the new site fails. Which approach will meet these requirements with the LEAST downtime for users?

options.label: A
options.text: On Saturday, lower the TTL of the A record to 300 seconds and replace it with an alias record for the load balancer in the same change.

options.label: B
options.text: Create a second public hosted zone for example.com with an alias record for the load balancer, and change the name servers at the registrar on Saturday.

options.label: C
options.text: On Saturday, replace the A record with an alias record for the load balancer, because Route 53 sends record changes to all of its servers within a minute.

options.label: D
options.text: Two days before Saturday, lower the TTL of the A record to 300 seconds; on Saturday, replace the record with an alias record for the load balancer.

items.stem: A company serves www.example.com from three Amazon EC2 instances that have Elastic IP addresses. Route 53 answers with three weighted A records, each with a nonzero weight and its own health check. During a failed deployment, all three instances failed their health checks, but users still received the addresses of the failed instances. When no instance is healthy, users must see a static error page from an S3 bucket named www.example.com that is configured as a website. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.label: A
options.text: Add a weighted alias record for the S3 website endpoint with a weight of 0, and remove the health checks from the three records so that failed instances are left out.

options.label: B
options.text: Lower the TTL of the three weighted records to 60 seconds, so that resolvers drop the failed addresses soon after Route 53 stops returning the unhealthy records.

options.label: C
options.text: Rename the three weighted records, then create failover records for www.example.com: an alias record for the weighted records as the primary, and the S3 website as the secondary.

options.label: D
options.text: Add a fourth weighted record for www.example.com: an alias record for the S3 website endpoint with a weight of 0, and keep the three records as they are.

items.stem: A company uses failover records in a Route 53 private hosted zone for an internal API. The primary record is an A record for the API, which runs on Amazon EC2 instances that have only private IP addresses. The secondary record points to a standby copy of the API. Route 53 must fail over to the secondary record when the primary API stops working. Which combination of steps will meet these requirements in the MOST secure way? (Select TWO.)

options.label: A
options.text: Assign public IP addresses to the primary instances, allow the health checker IP ranges in their security group, and check those public addresses.

options.label: B
options.text: Create a Route 53 HTTP health check that sends requests to the private IP address of one primary instance, and associate it with the primary record.

options.label: C
options.text: Create an Amazon CloudWatch metric that reflects the health of the primary API, and create a CloudWatch alarm that watches that metric.

options.label: D
options.text: Create a Route 53 health check that monitors the state of the CloudWatch alarm, and associate that health check with the primary record.

options.label: E
options.text: Add the IP ranges of the Route 53 health checkers to the security group of the primary instances, so that the health checkers can reach the API.

items.stem: A company runs the same stateless web application in us-east-1 and eu-west-1, behind an Application Load Balancer in each Region. The application has users around the world. The company hosts its DNS records in a Route 53 public hosted zone. Because of a data residency rule, users in Europe must be served from eu-west-1, and all other users from us-east-1. Which routing configuration for www.example.com will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.label: A
options.text: Weighted alias records for the two load balancers with equal weights, so that each Region receives half of the DNS queries for the name.

options.label: B
options.text: IP-based records with a CIDR collection that the team keeps current with the client IP ranges that each of the two Regions must serve.

options.label: C
options.text: Latency alias records for the two load balancers, one record in each Region, with Evaluate Target Health turned on for both records.

options.label: D
options.text: Geolocation alias records: a Europe record that points to the eu-west-1 load balancer, and a Default record for the us-east-1 load balancer.

items.stem: A company runs a web application on Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group behind an Application Load Balancer in us-east-1. A copy of the application runs the same way in us-west-2. A failed instance must be replaced automatically. When the whole application in us-east-1 fails, users must be sent to us-west-2. Which solution will provide a highly available design with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.label: A
options.text: Turn on ELB health checks for both Auto Scaling groups, and create failover alias records for the two load balancers with Evaluate Target Health on the primary.

options.label: B
options.text: Turn on ELB health checks for both Auto Scaling groups, and run a scheduled script that points the record to us-west-2 when the us-east-1 load balancer fails.

options.label: C
options.text: Turn on ELB health checks for both Auto Scaling groups, so that the us-east-1 load balancer sends users to us-west-2 when all of its targets fail.

options.label: D
options.text: Create a Route 53 health check for each instance, so that Route 53 replaces a failed instance and sends users to us-west-2 when every check fails.

items.stem: A company has a Route 53 public hosted zone for example.com with records for www.example.com and api.example.com. The company creates a private hosted zone named example.com, associates it with its production VPC, and adds a record for db.example.com. Currently, instances in the VPC resolve db.example.com but not api.example.com, so calls to the public API fail. The name db.example.com must stay private and must not change. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.label: A
options.text: Run DNS forwarder software on EC2 instances that answers db.example.com from a local zone file and forwards all other names to public DNS resolvers.

options.label: B
options.text: Set the VPC attributes enableDnsSupport and enableDnsHostnames to true, so that names missing from the private hosted zone are answered from the public hosted zone.

options.label: C
options.text: Create an outbound Resolver endpoint and a forwarding rule for example.com that sends the DNS queries of the VPC to a public DNS resolver on the internet.

options.label: D
options.text: Create api.example.com and the other public names that the instances use in the private hosted zone, with the same values as the public records.

items.stem: An application runs in us-east-1 and ap-southeast-1 behind an Application Load Balancer in each Region. Both Regions must serve users at all times. Each user must reach the Region with the lowest latency, and users must leave a Region whose application fails. The company wants a highly available cross-Region design that the team can run with little effort. Which Route 53 configuration is the MOST operationally efficient?

options.label: A
options.text: Latency alias records for the two load balancers, one record for each Region, with Evaluate Target Health set to Yes on both records.

options.label: B
options.text: Latency alias records for the two load balancers, and a Route 53 HTTP health check of each load balancer that is associated with its record.

options.label: C
options.text: Failover alias records for the two load balancers, with us-east-1 as the primary, ap-southeast-1 as the secondary, and Evaluate Target Health turned on.

options.label: D
options.text: Latency A records that hold the current IP addresses of each load balancer, with no health checks, because Route 53 skips a Region that stops answering.

items.stem: A company runs its own DNS servers for its public domain on two Amazon EC2 instances in one Availability Zone of the us-east-1 Region. The DNS servers answer queries from customers on the internet. The company wants a fully managed DNS service that keeps answering queries if an Availability Zone or a whole AWS Region fails. What should a solutions architect recommend?

options.label: A
options.text: Create a Route 53 private hosted zone for the domain, and associate it with VPCs in two AWS Regions.

options.label: B
options.text: Move the DNS servers to EC2 instances in two Availability Zones of us-east-1, behind a Network Load Balancer.

options.label: C
options.text: Create a Route 53 public hosted zone for the domain, and update the domain's name servers at the registrar.

options.label: D
options.text: Create inbound Resolver endpoints in two Availability Zones of us-east-1, and send the internet DNS queries to the endpoint addresses.

items.stem: A company runs a web application on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer. In the Route 53 public hosted zone, app.example.com is an A record that holds the IP addresses of the load balancer. An engineer copied the addresses when the load balancer was created. Users now report intermittent connection errors, mostly after traffic peaks. The company wants to stop the errors. Which solution is the MOST cost-effective way to meet these requirements?

options.label: A
options.text: Replace the A record with a CNAME record for app.example.com whose value is the DNS name that AWS assigned to the Application Load Balancer.

options.label: B
options.text: Associate Elastic IP addresses with the Application Load Balancer, and replace the values of the A record for app.example.com with those Elastic IP addresses.

options.label: C
options.text: Replace the A record with an alias record of type A for app.example.com that points to the Application Load Balancer.

options.label: D
options.text: Create a scheduled AWS Lambda function that reads the current load balancer addresses every minute and writes them into the A record for app.example.com.

items.stem: A company runs a TCP service on six Amazon EC2 instances across two Availability Zones in one Region. Clients connect to service.example.com, which is in a Route 53 public hosted zone. New connections must be spread evenly across the healthy instances. When an instance fails, it must stop receiving new connections at once, also from clients that cached a DNS answer earlier. Which solution will provide a highly available design with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.label: A
options.text: Create a Network Load Balancer with the six instances as targets in both Availability Zones, and an alias record for service.example.com that points to it.

options.label: B
options.text: Run open-source proxy software on two EC2 instances in different Availability Zones to spread connections and check the six instances, with a record for each proxy.

options.label: C
options.text: Create one simple A record for service.example.com that lists the IP addresses of all six instances, so that each client picks one address at random.

options.label: D
options.text: Create a multivalue answer record for each instance under service.example.com, and associate a Route 53 health check with each of the six records.

items.stem: A company uses a shared-services account to centrally manage a private hosted zone named internal.example.com. One VPC in a separate workload account must resolve the records of that zone, and the records must stay private. In the Route 53 console of the shared-services account, an engineer tries to associate the zone with the workload VPC but cannot find the VPC. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.label: A
options.text: Create a VPC peering connection between a VPC in the shared-services account and the workload VPC, so that the workload VPC can query the private hosted zone.

options.label: B
options.text: Authorize the association from the shared-services account with the AWS CLI, associate the VPC with the zone from the workload account, and then delete the authorization.

options.label: C
options.text: Replace the private hosted zone with a public hosted zone that has the same records, so that the workload VPC can resolve the names without an association.

options.label: D
options.text: Create a copy of the private hosted zone in the workload account, associate the copy with the workload VPC, and sync the records with a scheduled script.
